questions.question: What are the major characteristics of static aquaculture system?
questions.solution_html:
• No Water Flow or Continuous Exchange, Low or Moderate Stocking Density
  • Because water is not flowing, it cannot dilute wastes effectively, Dependence
  • on Natural Ecological Processes, natural food organisms (plankton), and self
  • purification processes of the pond ecosystem, Higher Risk of Water Quality
  • Fluctuations, Fertilizers (organic or inorganic) are added to increase natural
  • productivity, Accumulation of Metabolites and Waste, Periodic removal of
  • sludge or drying of ponds between cycles is required, Simple Infrastructure
  • and Low Input System, Often used in traditional aquaculture, rural farms, or
  • low-cost farming systems, Suitable for Hardy Species Eg: Carp, Tilapia
  • Catfish
  • Efficient use of existing water bodies, Easy management and harvesting, low
  • initial investment, high stocking density, better water exchange, easy
  • expansion, flexibility in species cultured (any two)
  • Water Quality Management : Aquaculture requires continuous monitoring and
  • control of parameters such as dissolved oxygen, pH, temperature, ammonia, nitrite
  • turbidity, and salinity.Even slight fluctuations can stress or kill fish, unlike crops
  • which can tolerate wider environmental variations.
  • Pond Dykes (Bunds)
  • Earthen embankments built around the pond.
  • Provide structural support and prevent water leakage.
  • Made with well-compacted clay soil.
  • Inner slopes are gentle (2:1) to prevent erosion.
  • Outer slopes may be steeper (1.5:1).
  • Dykes should be strong enough for movement of workers or vehicles.
  • Order: Salmoniformes
  • This order includes the true cold-water species known for their migratory behaviour
  • and high economic value.
  • Body Shape
  • Generally streamlined, fusiform bodies help reduce friction during swimming
  • in swift currents.
  • Trout and mahseer show powerful, muscular bodies for sustained swimming.
  • Trout and Salmon (Order: Salmoniformes)
  • Renowned worldwide for sport fishing.
  • Their strong, energetic movement and ability to jump make them ideal for
  • angling.
  • Strong Muscular Body
  • Well-developed muscles support powerful bursts of speed needed to escape
  • predators and resist capture.

questions.question: Discuss the effect of Turbidity on pond productivity
questions.solution_html:
• Turbidity reduces pond productivity by limiting the penetration of sunlight
  • into the water. This results in reduced oxygen levels and diminished natural
  • food availability for fish. High turbidity from suspended clay particles or
  • organic matter can also clog fish gills, stress the fish, and interfere with
  • feeding.
  • Faster Growth Rate, Higher Production, Better Feed Conversion Ratio (FCR)
  • Hardy and Disease-Resistant, Economically Beneficial, Adaptable to Various
  • Culture Systems
  • Short Answer Questions
  • Disease Outbreaks : Rapid spread of bacterial, viral, fungal, or parasitic infections
  • in dense stocking conditions.Fish live in a shared water medium; pathogens spread
  • faster than in terrestrial crops or livestock.
  • Inlet Structure
  • Allows controlled entry of water into the pond.
  • Fitted with screens or filters to prevent unwanted fish, predators, insects, and
  • debris from entering.
  • Must deliver water without disturbing the pond bottom.
  • Ideally located at a higher elevation than the outlet for gravity flow.
  • Order: Cypriniformes
  • Many snow-fed Himalayan streams harbour cyprinid cold-water fishes.
  • Family: Cyprinidae
  • Genera: Tor, Schizothorax
  • Important species
  • Mahseer (Tor putitora, Tor khudree), Snow trouts (Schizothorax spp.)
  • Mahseer is one of the most prestigious game fishes of India, known for its strength
  • and size.
  • Colouration
  • Cold-water fishes often display silvery, dark-mottled, or spotted patterns
  • providing camouflage in clear waters.
  • Rainbow trout exhibits a characteristic pink lateral band.
  • Mahseer (Order: Cypriniformes)
  • Considered the Tiger of Indian rivers
  • Exhibits explosive strength, making it a prized game fish.
  • Well-Developed Caudal Peduncle
  • A narrow but sturdy caudal peduncle increases thrust during fast swimming.
questions.final_answer: A narrow but sturdy caudal peduncle increases thrust during fast swimming

questions.question: Define Sewage Fed Fish Culture
questions.solution_html:
• Sewage-fed fish culture is an aquaculture practice in which treated or partially
  • treated sewage water is used to grow fish in specially managed ponds. The
  • nutrients present in sewage, mainly organic matter, nitrogen, and
  • phosphorus promote the growth of phytoplankton, zooplankton, and other
  • natural fish food organisms, which support fish production.
  • Risk of Escape and Biodiversity Issues: Farmed fish may escape into natural water
  • bodies and compete with or hybridize with wild fish.Agriculture rarely causes such
  • ecological impacts; escapees can disrupt native aquatic ecosystems.
  • Water Supply and Drainage System
  • Must ensure constant water availability.
  • Should allow water exchange without disturbing fish.
  • Efficient drainage prevents stagnation and reduces disease risk.
  • Collection of sludge
  • Movement of fish during harvest
  • Mouth and Feeding Adaptations
  • Salmonids possess a terminal mouth with sharp teeth for carnivorous feeding.
  • Mahseer shows a sub-terminal mouth with thick, fleshy lips for scraping food
  • from rocks.
  • Strong Dentition
  • Helps grasp live prey, making them aggressive and challenging game species.
questions.final_answer: Helps grasp live prey, making them aggressive and challenging game species
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
